title: PA degrees

based_on.title: Computability theory
based_on.pages: 87 (§23.2, Theorem 23.7; version 2024-02-25). Arithmetic representation, proof-search and tree-selector arguments are expanded in the corpus's fixed languages and numberings.

summary: Characterize the oracles computing complete consistent extensions of Peano arithmetic by binary diagonal avoidance and paths through computable binary trees.
abstract: An oracle can help choose a consistent arithmetic answer to every sentence by deciding which of a sentence and its negation to retain. The oracles able to complete Peano arithmetic in this way are exactly those computing a zero-one function that disagrees with every defined program on that program's own index. They are also exactly those able to choose an infinite path through every computable binary tree with an infinite path. The arithmetic direction uses finite comparisons of computation certificates, while the reverse construction makes each choice by avoiding the output of a program searching for a contradiction. Some of these oracles lie strictly below the halting problem, and every oracle that solves the halting problem has this ability.
